analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING: 1) FX Trader Call Today, 2) September CPI Preview, 3) Hybrids: Stretched Equity/Rates Correlation, 4) 5 Key Charts and 5) GS Energy Webcast
key_insights: GS US economics forecasts September core CPI at +0.24% m/m (consensus +0.2%) and +2.46% y/y (consensus +2.5%). Headline CPI is forecast at +0.59% (consensus +0.6%), driven by higher energy prices. This is consistent with a 0.20% core PCE increase in September.

Component forecasts for September CPI: used cars +0.5%, new cars +0.2%, auto insurance +0.2%, OER +0.20%, rent +0.17%, airfares +3.0% on higher jet fuel prices. Shelter is expected to stay benign as underlying trends slow.

GS expects core CPI of about 0.2% m/m in October, with upward pressure from seasonal-factor distortions caused by missing data from last year's government shutdown. It expects about 0.1% in November and December as shelter slows and tariff-related price increases shrink.

GS estimates AI price pressures currently add about 45bp to core PCE inflation, about half of it genuine rather than mismeasurement. The impact is expected to peak at 50bp by end-2026 and fall to 10bp by end-2027. The effect on headline PCE is about 5-10bp higher over that horizon. The decline next year reflects slower expected growth in memory and computer prices.

GS Hybrids desk says flows hedging downside AI tails have pushed the equity/yield correlation back to highs. Implied SPX-US yields correlation is +10 on 6m, while realised is about -50% on 6m and -40% on 1m and 3m.

The Hybrids desk proposes dual-asset trades to exploit the gap between implied and realised correlation: a rates-relief/equity-higher trade on SPX or KOSPI2, a European energy-shock trade on SX5E vs 2y EUR rates, and a small-cap trade on RTY vs 2y SOFR.
Chart 1 of the 5 Key Charts: average yields in major developed markets are up 100-120bps across the curve YTD, the highest levels since 2007.
Chart 2: household consumption in Australia and Sweden is most affected by higher rates. A 100bp rise in yields would cut consumer spending by more than 1%.
Charts 3 and 4 cover UK public opinion on rejoining the EU, showing increased support for a closer relationship, and the options for closer UK-EU relations.
Chart 5: the AAPL vs NDX rolling 22-day correlation points to the defensive nature of the rally in AAPL.

GS hosts an FX Trader Call at 2:00 PM London covering G10 and EM flow and trade ideas. Will Marshall's piece 'The Factors Behind the Rise in US Yields' is flagged, with G10 spot and vol traders participating.
GS energy webcast at 3pm London covers oil and nat gas forecasts, geopolitical risk and winter weather impact on forecasts.
